patch.value: Public git history embeds a personal author email and blocks release approval

A full reachable-history identity scan found that every current commit stores a personal email in author and often committer metadata. The repository is already public, so fixing the raw history requires a coordinated history rewrite and force update, not a mailmap-only cosmetic change. No token, private-key, local-path, or LAN-address patterns were found by the current scan.

Choose a public noreply identity; rewrite all reachable branches and tags plus audit unreachable objects; independently scan the rewritten object database and working tree; coordinate force updates and invalidate stale clones; verify GitHub, npm provenance, changelog links, and PR refs; document the migration without publishing the removed personal value.
Publishing releases before remediation would preserve personal data in every distributed clone and package provenance link.

patch.value: Correction after a policy-level audit on 2026-08-07: the apparent local pass did not prove the coordinated rewrite succeeded. The approved-identity file itself still allowlisted a maintainer personal address, contradicting this item's explicit rule that allowlisting must not convert a privacy blocker into approval. The remote mirror's additional rejected address belongs to Dependabot's public GitHub noreply identity on closed dependency PR refs #13-#15 and is safe to approve. The allowlist now contains only GitHub public service/noreply identities, and audit:identities again fails closed on the remaining personal address. This P0 remains open until the raw history is actually rewritten and pruned.

Superseded by the maintainer's standing decision (2026-07-21, reaffirming an earlier closed decision): stefan@preu.at is the maintainer's approved public authoring identity for this fleet, present in the public history of every unbraind/pm-* repo, and must NOT be rewritten or purged. The full public history rewrite this item demanded was a manufactured release blocker written by an agent that did not know the decision. The approved-identity file now distinguishes an approved public authoring identity (allowlisted) from an unapproved identity (still fails closed), and adds stefan@preu.at with a citing comment. audit:identities now passes; a new test proves an unapproved identity is still rejected, so the gate is not a rubber stamp.
